utterances.text: This is again an article from Kozarski Vjesnik dated 30th May 1994. It is headlined: "Staff changes in IBC (the Information and Business Centre) Kozarski Vjesnik, new manager Slobodan Kuruzovic".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this document for admission as 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 102 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be displayed on the screen? If we could go back and look at the third paragraph. Looking at the third paragraph, Dr. Greve, does it indicate Slobodan Kuruzovic's position in the Serbian TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last sentence in paragraph 3 refers to him, Slobodan Kuruzovic, as being the Commander of Serbian Territorial Defence headquartered in Prijedor and one of the organisers of the seizure of power in Prijedor on 29th/30th April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does it indicate whether or not he was also a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Mr. Kuruzovic was commander of the Serbian Territorial Defence headquarters in Prijedor and had assisted in organising the military takeover of Prijedor, what position was he appointed to according to this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this article, he is becoming head of the Kozarski Vjesnik which at this point has long been a mark piece of the Serbian propaganda and information efforts in opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at the last line of the article, does Mr. Kuruzovic indicate the principles by which he will be guided in running Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does. "The orthodox creed, the interests of Serbian people in Republika Srpska will be the main guidelines for my editorial policies in IBC, said Kuruzovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, I would like to bring your attention to the period of time immediately before the military takeover of Prijedor at the end of April 1992. First of all, let me ask you briefl about the political situation within Prijedor at that stage. Was the Municipal Assembly functioning effectively and as a working democratic institution at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not, but let me perhaps add that there was an Executive Board with secretariats that did function, although the Assembly with its committees did not function or not function very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the opstina was not completely broken down, but were political decisions being made in the normal fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was running as a political entity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was happening within the Assembly at that point? How effectively was it functioning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not functioning effectively. It was being obstructed. It was almost impossible to reach a consensus on anything and there were occasions where participants would leave the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the mechanisms were still available but decisions could not be made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had a separate Assembly been established by that time by Serbs in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it had, as it was illustrated earlier by the decision that they wanted to join the autonomous region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And had the separate police stations been established by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the military situation at that point, had troops or reservists who had gone or volunteers who had gone to fight in Croatia returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the majority had returned and even more than the people who came from Prijedor. There was a cease-fire in Croatia early in 1991, and because Prijedor has this infrastructure and link between the regions in Croatia where the battles had been fought, all the troops that withdrew through Bosnia-Herzegovina or a large number of those troops necessarily would be withdrawn through Prijedor. That is not exactly the corridor but it is this important link by road from these Croatian battlefields and to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were those persons who had been mobilized or volunteered to fight in Croatia, primarily of one ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority were Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When they returned were they demobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they retain their arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were additional troops beyond those persons who were originally from the opstina placed in or near opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is to say, some of them had been placed when the war in Croatia was already on and the people will claim that, "This was our troops, so we were not afraid of them", they were placed locally and it was said that possibly they would move on to Croatia if they were needed on the battlefield, and they just were stationed in Prijedor. Others when going back did not leave Prijedor but stayed on for a while in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had heavy weaponry been brought into the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a lot of heavy weaponry, such as tanks, howitzers, artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there paramilitary troops in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the origins of some of those troops known to citizens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I may perhaps explain at this point that there are two main variations to my understanding of the Serbo Croatian language; it is Ekavian which is spoken essentially in Serbia, and Ijekavian which is spoken in Croatia and Bosnia. Again, I do not know the language, but it is explained to me that the difference is equal to that between British-English and American-English, so that people will immediately be able to distinguish if a person speaks the Ekavinin language which is found in Serbia proper. But there are exceptions. There are some areas in Serbia proper which speaks the same Ijekavian language as the people in Croatia and Bosnia, but not the other way round, according to the dictionaries which I have consulted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally, were Serb civilians armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened on the night April 29th, April 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the very early hours of 30th April, that is after midnight, approximately 4 o'clock, the Serbs in opstina Prijedor, co-operation between army, including paramilitary forces, police and the party, were seizing power with armed force; that is, they established all over the town of Prijedor checkpoints, placed armed guards outside all the main buildings, police station, bank, town hall and inside the radio station, etc., etc., and ha snipers on the roofs. They also went public on Radio Prijedor to announce that they had by force established Srpske opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now did the de facto Serbian authorities later claim that the takeover was triggered by some particular event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. When journalists spoke, well, I should say this, that the people living in opstina Prijedor at this time, as mentioned yesterday, had been cut off from receiving TV transmissions and broadcasts from Sarajevo. They would only see the broadcasts that came from Belgrade, Banja Luka or eventually Pale. The TV station in Belgrade had on 29th April transmitted a facsimile of a telefax to the effect that the Republic -- the leader of TO in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had given an instruction to the TO in Bosnia-Herzegovina to attack and obstruct the JNA when they were to withdraw from Bosnia-Herzegovina. But immediately this telefax was denounced and declared false by the authorities in Sarajevo, and I have not come across people who have actually had themselves access to this telefax in Prijedor. However, when journalists later came to Banja Luka, they were given a copy of this telefax as the pretext why this power change had to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 103? (Document handed). What is that document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is called FBIS EEU 92084, of 30th April 1992 -- FBIS EEU is the Foreign Broadcast Information Service Eastern Europe -- and it is referring to a broadcast which was made by radio Sarajevo network in Serbo-Croatian at 1818 GMT, 29th April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 103 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Does this document indicate whether or not Bosnian authorities were aware of reports that an order had been given to local TOs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it indicates that they were informed of this and they thus had to come out immediately to state that this was false.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does the exhibit indicate whether or not a public denunciation of that fax as false was made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is referring to such denunciation already having been made and it is repeating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: In fact, Dr. Greve, did the de facto Serbian officials of Prijedor indicate themselves whether or not the takeover was a spontaneous event in response to this fax or, in fact, a long-standing plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are consistently referring to a long-standing plan. At one point they speak about why it had to be the 9th to 30th; they are saying that, "We had it considered to make it the 30th, the night after this night to 1st of May, but because of this we had to move forward 24 hours". But I should also add that years after this happened, there is no more any mention of this telefax. However, there is reference to a completely different telefax to which no mention was made in the early days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask that Exhibit 91 be placed before the witness? If I can ask you to look at the third paragraph, does this indicate whether or not the takeover was a spontaneous reaction or a planned event for some time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It clearly states that this was not a spontaneous reaction; it was only the final act of a long-standing plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: The person who says this is whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was he the first Chairman of the Serbian Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May document Exhibit 90 be placed in front of the witness once more? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, you indicated that the takeover was a co-ordinated effort between political police and military authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does paragraph 3 of Exhibit 93 indicate who participated in the takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does that article say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This paragraph refers, if I should take at this point only the second half of it, "It was not easy to hold illegal meetings and to prepare for defence, but after the presidency of the former BIH blockaded the barracks and other military installations, it was decided in agreement with the officers of the Serbian army, the Serbian Democratic Party and the Executive Committee of the Municipality of Prijedor to seize power from the Muslim extremists"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this takeover which took place by force of arms on April 30th 1992, with the agreement and co-operation of the JNA, was that before the announced withdrawal of JNA troops from Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: They were the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims physically resist when confronted by the arms, the combined arms, of the JNA, the Serbian police, the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not, and I assume that is why it can also be stated here in the article, in the next paragraph, that all this happened without one shot being fired, and that is repeatedly referred to in newspaper articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that connection, can I draw your attention back to Exhibit 100? In Exhibit 100, does Simo Miskovic indicate whether or not there was Muslim or Croat resistance to the takeover on April 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo Miskovic is stating that on 30th April 1992 the takeover was achieved without a single shot being fired and without a single casualty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, I would next like to ask you about the immediate consequences of this takeover. First of all, did it have an effect on the dissemination of propaganda or information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Immediately, both Kozarski Vjesnik and radio Prijedor became virtual mouth-pieces of the new authorities, that is, the Srpska opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there an escalation of the tenor or the tone of that propaganda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the terms used for Croats and Muslim became much more derogative.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there an effect on the movement for Muslims and Croats within the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, movement for these groups was severely obstructed, but I should perhaps say that when one refers to Muslim and Croats, it is perhaps even more correct to refer to non-Serbs because there were other tiny minority groups who were also not included in the Serb group. Among Serbs were considered also the Montenegrins, there were not many of them, but they were like smaller brothers, and there were some of the aliens who were well accepted, but, essentially, it was the Serbs and the non-Serbs of whom the Muslims were the majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the nature of the control of movement within the opstina, how was it affected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several measures being implemented. There were road blocks at intersections where people would have to show their IDs, and if their ID card would not prove them to be Serbs, then they could not been identified as Serbs, they were not necessarily entitled to pass the road blocks. They would need special permits to travel, and it was very limited and restricted where were they were able to travel. They could no longer leave opstina Prijedor, essentially. They also had to abide by a curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Serbian officials later acknowledge just how tight these controls became?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention back to Exhibit 99, please? Directing your attention to page 3 of that document, looking at the middle of that page where there is a statement by Mr. Ecim, does he indicate in any way how tight some of those controls became?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does indeed, because he is referring to the difficulties, well, actually he is placing blame on some Serbs who assisted, allegedly, Muslims to leave or non-Serbs to leave, saying that they were leaving the region in coffins, in cars owned by the Serbs and with Serbian IDs which indicates it was not an easy thing to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a control of communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was control of communication. It is recalled that there are some main roads going through the area and it was no more possible for the non-Serbian population to have bus tickets to leave, and they could not leave with their own cars least they had had Serbian IDs, and they could not easily get a ticket, if at all, on the railway, and there is an aerodrome in the area, but it is not a modern airport, it is more like a sports field for sports planes and there were no regular air traffic through the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about the use of telephones, did that change in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were on and off the telephone lines were blocked for the non-Serbs. This soon became more the general rule than the exception and also electricity was in part shut down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the takeover, was there an effect on the employment status of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, actually, and this is later being confirmed by the official gazette by the autonomous region of Krajina, now it became important to be a good Serb, someone who knew that and had demonstrated that they were loyal to the Serbs, the party, the plebiscite had voted for independence etc., and this definitely meant that all the non-Serbs would no more qualify for leading positions and they were asked to leave all leading positions Eventually, within days, the majority of the workforce, even in factories, were asked to leave their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this document marked as Exhibit 104 for identification, please? (Document handed). (To the witness): What is this document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a full translation of a newspaper article. It is not mentioned where it is published in the translation, but it mentioned that the date of publication is 22nd June 1992, and its headline is "Leaders - only loyal Serbs!". Within this article there is a facsimile from a decision made by the autonomous region of Krajina. It is Crisis Staff in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 104 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Can that be raised a bit? Dr. Greve, does this document indicate whether or not the process of termination from the employment of Muslims and Croats which began after the takeover continued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it indicates that this continued and it was more and more demands being made concerning those who were to keep positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does it also indicate the conditions or qualifications for continued positions, important positions, within the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This is the time when virtually most of the non-Serbian population has already been asked to leave their jobs. Now, the remaining ones are Serbs, and it is being indicated that any Serb is not good enough. It is stated that in addition to being of Serbian nationality -- I am looking at the second paragraph, the second part -- "In addition they", that is the Serb nationals, "must have confirmed their Serbian nationality in the plebiscite". That is the one, 9th and 10th November 1991, and it must be ideologically clear to them that the only representative of the Serbian people is the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if I can ask a question about this? I see the reference here to the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was at a time when it had been declared that a Serbian Republic would remain part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Could one have a separate army if one was a Republic of the Yugoslav nation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, no, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did the other entities of that rump nation have their own armies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eventually, they moved to establish their own armies and armed entities but, as was illustrated yesterday with the decision made by the committee of senior officials in the then conference on co-operation and security in Europe, it was pointed out in that decision that the heavy equipment belonging to the JNA had to be withdrawn, as had all the personnel that did not belong to Bosnia or come originally from Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that it could not simply be up to the JNA to decide to establish a Bosnian-Serb army, give them full armament etc.; either the arms had to be withdrawn from Bosnia-Herzegovina or it had to be placed under the control of the legal authorities, that is, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the new de facto Serbian authorities following the takeover begin to make demands on the Muslim and Croat population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the nature of those demands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the first demands was in a sense a follow-up, if I may mention, of what had happened already previously or prior to taking power; that is, that non-Serbs who for one reason or the other had a weapon, they were being approached by police or tanks or anyone. Although this might be a hunting rifle and they may have a licence for carrying that hunting rifle, they were asked to give up their arms. They were told if they did not accept to give it up, they will be forced to give it up. So many people had started to hand in whatever hunting weapons they had, or other weapons if they were members of sports clubs, handling weapons or whatever. But this was speeded up considerably after the Serbs took power. Then they made a demand that everyone who had any kind of weapons should hand them over immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In general, how did the Muslim and Croat community respond to those demands to surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By and large, I believe most of those weapons were handed into the Serbs because they were confronted with an overwhelming strength of arms. However, there were people who were appointed policemen by the legal authorities in Sarajevo who were not necessarily immediately willing to give up their arms to an illegal entity; there was a conflict of loyalty in this situation. They were appointed as representatives of a legal government, and they did not, all of them, immediately give up their arms. The same was the case with this not so good arms kept by some of the Territorial Defence. They were also in this; they were a part of a legal structure and immediately to hand over their weapons to an illegal entity was not always done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the de facto Serb authorities demand any demonstration or pledge of loyalty to their new regime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Before virtually dismissing all the police, they called them for meetings and said they would have to carry the new Serbian insignia, they would have to pledge loyalty to the new Srpska opstina Prijedor, etc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the schools function normally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially, yes, but it was decided (and that is also confirmed by the decision made by the autonomous region of Krajina) that this particular year they would end school much earlier than normally. They would end on 20th May which, I think, is a significant date for the later events. This is also the time when virtually everyone in the Serb population had been mobilized to the army, to the reserve, to the police, to the Reserve Police Force, and this way also the teachers became available to take up service also in the Territorial Defence Forces of which the Serbs had their special branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Schools were closed by order of the autonomous region Krizni Stab on May 20th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did the first military action against a Muslim or Croat community take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 22nd May. If I may add also one thing, already during the mobilization for Croatia, it had become a problem that there were not enough military uniforms when they tried to get everyone into uniform. So it seems that on occasions many people would go to war partly dressed in uniform and partly in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit 78 displayed? I apologise. Apparently, Exhibit 79 will better illustrate the region for the witness. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, can you show us the area where the first military attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is on this stretch from Prijedor and up to Hambarine which is located on a higher level than Prijedor, the town, and Hambarine is one village, but it is also a Mjesna Zajednica which includes areas to its north and west, essentially -- also some to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there any incident which preceded the military attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was. Hambarine is located on the way towards Ljubija -- this road actually continues down to Ljubija -- and Ljubija was an area which at that time had not been -- the full Serbian control had not yet been established; that is, as we will return to later, on the day of 22nd May, the Serbs claimed that once again they took power in Ljubija without any violence, they just being cunning (as they are saying themselves) were able to get all the weapons away from all the non-Serbs in that area. But, at this day there was a road block on the road from Prijedor up to Hambarine, manned by some Muslim people, and there was a car coming up, I believe it was, according to newspaper articles referring to this later, four Serbs and one Croat in this car; the Croat being the driver, the Serbs possibly being members of the Bijeliorlovi which is the White Eagles which is a paramilitary unit. They were in uniform and they were carrying arms and they were asked to stop at this check point to give up their arms before they passed. Apparently, they did not want to do that and there was a shooting incident in which two Serbs were killed; one of the Muslims was initially wounded and subsequently died from his wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Following that incident, was there an ultimatum made on the residents of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an ultimatum that Hambarine as such would have to hand over to the authorities in Prijedor town, it was announced on radio Prijedor, the three or four people who had actually been manning this checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the ultimatum expired the next day, what happened? Was there a military attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a military attack. Compared to what was later to come, this was not an extreme attack. It was an attack whereby Hambarine area and nearby locations were initially shelled by heavy artillery, some of which were stationed in the town of Prijedor at the airfield, aerodrome, Urije, in that area, so they were actually shooting from across Prijedor and up to Hambarine. When the bombardment ended, the Serb armed entities came with tanks and other weaponry to the area of Hambarine. Many of the people had already left this area going either north to Rizvanovici, Biscani and other villages in this area which at this point were not that much attacked, and they had tried to withdraw to the south which is a forested area -- it is called Kurevo -- and that was being shelled as well as the people left.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, yesterday I tendered document 82 with the understanding that it was a black and white copy of a document we expected to receive in full colour shortly. That document is here and it can be used today.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. That is 88?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 82, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 82, sorry. Is there any objection to the colour being substituted for what was admitted yesterday as 82?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. It will be substituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May the new document 82 be displayed for the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, you explained this map to us yesterday when it was only depicted in black and white. Perhaps you can indicate to us quickly what the colours represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The colour code will be that the green indicates predominantly or mainly Muslim habitations and settlements, the blue indicates the Serb ones and the red indicates the Croat ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you indicate then on this map of the ethnic distribution of opstina Prijedor where the region you were talking about before the adjournment or the recess is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We then was looking at Hambarine which is both a village and a Mjesna Zajednica which covers adjacent areas as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that on May 23rd Hambarine was subjected to first shelling and then troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Invaded by troops and tanks, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did the residents of Hambarine do when the shelling began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tried to run away, run to the north, to other Muslim areas, or to the south, still to Muslim areas; and the Carakovo which is indicated here, that is in a forested area as well, so it is possibly easier to hide to the south than to the north, but it was shelling also in the Carakavo area for those who fled to the forest. That eventually led to a number of people seeking even further to the southwest, to the area marked as Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the residents of the area eventually return to the Hambarine area

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite a number did return. It should be remembered, though, that there had been ethnic cleansing going out outside of opstina Prijedor, in opstina Bosanski Novi, to the west, that this, so some people had come into opstina Prijedor and, essentially, come to settle in this western/southern part of opstina Prijedor with people who were Muslims or who were Croats as again in Bosanski Novi the people who were ethnically cleansed were the non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The residents who fled that initial shelling of Hambarine and the invasion of troops, and then returned, did they eventually leave the area again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at a later stage they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. We will come to that in the course of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that after this initial attack on Hambarine on May 23rd some of the residents fled to the Ljubija area which is also depicted on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. It is this area. It is actually divided in two settlements. It is called Donja Ljubija and Gornja Ljubija; "donja" is lower and "gornja" is upper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there weapons available in Ljubija at the TO headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the residents of Hambarine who fled to the Ljubija area gather up those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened to those weapons that were in the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the Serb chronicles of what happened in Ljubija at this time, the Serbs succeeded in taking hand of all these weapons immediately before they ever been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked for identification as Exhibit 105? (Document handed).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: You raised my expectations; I thought you were going to give each of us a coloured map, not so?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had the same hope, your Honour, but I understand, based on discussions, we can scan that document this evening, and produce colour copies from the printed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what is Exhibit 105?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This exhibit is once again an article from Kozarski Vjesnik. It is dated June 17th 1994, and it is a series of articles and it is set in connection with May 22nd when Serbian rule was established in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We would tender that document for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 105 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, can I ask you to look at the second page of that document -- actually perhaps we had better place it in context. Would you look at the first page? In the bottom of the first paragraph, does it indicate what happened after the attack on Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it referred to the fact that mostly non-Serbian population lived in the environs of Ljubija and they were well-armed. In Ljubija itself, there was a Territorial Defence unit which had only three Serbs. All the extremists from the left side of the Sana, that is the river that flows on the left side of this area, hid in the woods around Ljubija and in the wake of May 22nd, 1992 refugees started pouring into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does the article go on to disclose what happened to the weapons in Ljubija which were, according to the article, guarded by only three Serbs -- if you could turn to page 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the bottom of the page, does that indicate what happened to those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it referred to the fact that the local leader of the Crisis Committee, his name being Slobodan Taranjac, concludes that the only real danger they, meaning the people in the Ljubija area, still faced was from the Territorial Defence, because it was largely made up of non-Serbs, and it is referring that as being yet another problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did the leader of the Serbian Territorial Defence find it necessary to rest those weapons from the non-Serbs weapons of the TO with force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he decided it would be enough to resort to cunning behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: How were those weapons extracted from the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you want me to have the third page of the article?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first paragraph on this page explains it. Do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is stating that they resorted to cunning: "I sent Krivi to tell the Territorial Defence that we were being attacked by 150 green berets; that Ivica Milosevic and his men had placed themselves under my command and that we were defending Ljubija. About 30 minutes later I sent Milo Gliga in his van to pick up the weapons from members of the Territoria Defence. He asked me how he was going to disarm them and I told him they had already done it themselves, because they would not defend Ljubija. Then Gliga arrived at Territorial Defence headquarters. He found Krivi there alone with all the weapons. That is how we eliminated yet another danger without firing a bullet."

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: So, according to the article, Krivi walked in and took the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, took care of the arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Would you look at page 1, there is a reference to a military unit there, the commander of which told them, the 43rd Brigade, not to open a front. What Brigade is that? What sort of unit is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If it helps your Honour, we will be submitting documentation which indicates what the 43rd was and where it operated during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we see the exhibit 82 again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The article which we just saw on the screen there -- I should perhaps have mentioned then -- also referred to 8,000 refugees coming into the Ljubija area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, the ethnic distribution indicates a large area depicted in green representing a large concentration of the Muslim population in the Hambarine area. Looking to the right, is there also, or was there also, a large concentration of the Muslim community of Prijedor in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was the possibly largest concentration of Muslim people in this area. The larger Kozarac area or the Potkozarac area, it is the mountain of Kozarac which is up, that is why there are no Serbian settlements up in the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe you indicated this earlier, but approximately how many people lived in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that larger area, including also down to Trnopolje and to Kevljani, there would be approximately 27,000 people of non-Serbian origin.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What region is this now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the larger region of Kozarac, Kozarac being this location, but it is often referred to as one larger area, the Kozarac area. The mountain is called Kozara and it runs up the entire length.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I thought you were talking about the entire Prijedor region opstina; I understand now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we call up photos 5/0101 followed by 5/0102 and 03? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what does this depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, this is a post card and it actually shows the mosque in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next picture, please? What does this picture depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again it is my understanding that it is another picture from Kozarac, and it shows the Marsala Tito which is the main street which crosses the two streets running Prijedor, Banja Luka, the old and the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next picture, please? Does this picture depict another shot of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender these for admission as Exhibit 106 and we do so in the form of this single document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 106 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what sort of town was Kozarac, what did the people do primarily? How prosperous was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a prosperous area. It was located close to the mountain of Kozara. It was an area which had sawmills and some timber activities. It was an intersection, a cross-road. It was the access road up to the main war memorial on the Kozara mountain, and a number of people in this area had been working abroad as foreign workers and had had some financial means to establish themselves with small businesses, etc. So it was considered to be a prosperous area within a, generally speaking, prosperous opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: After the armed takeover of opstina Prijedor, did the de facto Serbian authorities make demands or ultimatums on the Kozarac community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They did demand that the TO also in this area would immediately pay respect, be subordinate to, the new authorities in Srpska opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any demand made on police officials in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same as on every police official in the opstina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did negotiations take place between the representatives of Kozarac community and the de facto authorities in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were those negotiations successful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly the participants thought they were successful to a certain degree and did expect them to go on but, as it all turned out, they were not successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did the demand for a pledge of loyalty by the police and the TO to the new Serbian authority continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was there a demand for disarmament?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did that continue to be made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: How well armed was the Kozarac community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were weapons with the police and there were weapons with the Territorial Defence forces, and there were a number of Muslims who had bought weapons if they could as they saw others being armed. But, generally speaking, there was very limited arms as compared to the arms available to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more question about the oath of loyalty that was demanded by de facto Serbian leaders. That would be an oath to be loyal to the new Serbian authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as being a party to this separate structure and separate Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Would it mean that the people of Kozarac would no longer be part of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: After the demand for surrender of arms and after the demand for a pledge of loyalty to the new officials, was Kozarac attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: When did that begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is my understanding that it started on 24th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: How did the attack on Kozarac begin, using what sort of military force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This time it was very heavy bombardment of the entire area. If we can have again perhaps the map of -----

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could exact Exhibit 79, 2/35? If the court is looking on the screen, it is a little difficult to read so perhaps you can orientate us before you describe -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Kozarac; this is the town of Prijedor; this is the mountainous area behind; these are the main roads Prijedor, Banja Luka; this is the fish farm, lake; yes, these are the basics that one needs just at this point to have an understanding. When Kozarac was attacked it is combined information from, well, actually all sources will indicate that it was attacked and bombarded from several different areas. Some were across -- or maybe I should start, there are proper military installations, long-term military installations, on the top of the Mountain Kozara. There were several installations on this mountain that were used to bombard Kozarac and nearby areas. However, there were also installations, to my understanding, placed somewhere in this area, the Kamen area, I understand, from the other side of the fish farm or the lake, Topjka Brdo and in some other areas here, Racelici, perhaps. That is that the people in Kozarac felt as if they were bombarded from every side at the same time and it was heavy bombardment with all kinds of heavy artillery which was only available, or had only been available, to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: How long did that heavy bombardment continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The immediate heavy bombardment continued for about 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Then did it stop entirely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did it continue intermittently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: For approximately how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For approximately up to 12 hours, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What did the residents of Kozarac do when the bombardment began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seek shelter, essentially, that is to say, some would immediately try to find the best cellar in the area, their own house or a neighbouring house; others would try to move towards the foot of the mountain although they were being shelled from the top of the mountain. This is as it is read out of the map, slightly hilly and they probably thought it would be safe in some of these areas. But as people moved up to the foot of the mountain the shelling also focused on the foot of the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: After the shelling ceased, what happened militarily after the shelling ceased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, there was one co-ordinated operation where several units were working together. It was ordinary military units with reserves and paramilitaries and police and reserves, and some local Serbs -- this was the time when about every adult male Serb was in uniform -- and moving in from different directions on the roads would come tanks and troops, and they would start attacking some of the different localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: That happened to the residents of Kozarac after the troops moved in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were forced to leave their houses, their shelters and asked to come out into the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Once they gathered in the streets, where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken to some points of, to where they were to be gathered and concentrated. Those who were from the centre of Kozarac were taken, essentially, in the direction of Kozarusa; some were also taken down on this main road towards Trnopolje, as we will come back to. The people were then separated so that women with small children up to 12, 15, and the elderly men, 60, 65 in this context, would be one group and the male population between 12, 15 or 60, 65, would be another group. A number of people were killed in the process -- we will come back to that, I think -- but those who were not killed were separated like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did the destruction of Kozarac end with the cessation of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see video footage taken by journalists who visited the Prijedor area in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I also spoke with some NGOs who were let into the area when it was almost so-called cleansed of non-Serbs who travelled through on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Have you seen recent footage of the Kozarac area or footage recently taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen footage taken by the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Is that also the most comprehensive footage of the area which you have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does it include both sides of the street, of the main street, that you showed us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does it include portions of both the main highway and the old road going in the direction both toward Omarska and toward Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I have been told and it corresponds to information I have from other sources but I have not been there, but maybe I should say that when the area had been cleansed and when it had been bombarded or bombarded and cleansed, each and every property which belonged to non-Serbs were, essentially, pillaged and then they were blown up from inside. So all the damage that could be seen on this footage is not due to the bombardment; it is also later activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we play video No. 5 at this time? Before we start it, the video is a portion of the footage taken all of which has been made available to the Defence. The extract is approximately 40 minutes long. It is not my intention to play the entire extract to the court at this time. I am sure the court will be interested in seeing it at a time more convenient, but I will play a portion of that before we stop the tape. I would like that marked for identification as 107 then.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Prosecution 107?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 107 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, this is the main street of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is this the mosque depicted in the photograph we saw earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Has the vehicle from which this video was taken now left the main portion of the town and proceeding up the road leading up to the mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, this section of the video is back down from the mountain leading back to town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was the Prijedor Banja Luka highway where the video ended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we stop the video, please? Your Honour, as I indicated, the video which was just an extract from a longer video goes on for approximately 45 minutes depicting similar scenes of destruction along the old road on both sides leading in the direction of Prijedor, on the Prijedor, Banja Luka highway on both sides leading towards Prijedor on that same highway and going toward the Omarska area and the old road going towards the Omarska area. There are just two additional questions I want to ask Dr. Greve about that, and then I will leave it to the court to review at its convenience. (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does the video to your recollection depict this Serbian orthodox church in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is the church damaged or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No single sign of damage is shown in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the video also depict the Serbian village of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That can be shown at the end of the video. What is the condition of Omarska village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is intact; it has not been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, after the Muslims and Croats of the Kozarac area were rounded up and segregated, where were the men of that area taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men were taken to two camps that were opened, one in Prijedor City, which is the one that is referred to as "Keraterm", and the other one just to the south of Omarska village, and that is referred to as "Omarska".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a third camp in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a third camp in the area and that is actually the railway station for Kozarac. It is also called Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could call up 2/35-2 on the computer screen, and could we have a zoom on the Omarska area in the upper right-hand corner? Dr. Greve, does this exhibit depict the location of Omarska village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the central of Omarska village, according to the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could hand back the original of the exhibit, please? First of all, I would like to tender that map as No. 108.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 108 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do I need to request for that to be printed? Thank you. (To the witness): Just to orientate us here, Dr. Greve, as I look up on the top portion of the map to the left side, does that show a small corner of the fish farm you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is this one -- should there be an arrow? I do not know how I make this -----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You may want to return, if necessary, I am just trying to orientate us according to the map we saw earlier that showed Prijedor and Omarska which is Exhibit 79.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we see the village of Omarska which is linked again through to the railroad that leads the whole way up to Prijedor, and we see the lake, the fish farm, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is the location of the camp that was established in the Omarska area depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my understanding, it is not. It is two kilometres south of Omarska village, and the scale of this map is that every square is 500 metre by 500 metre, so it is two kilometres to the south, slightly to the west of Omarska city, I understand, or village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it located near any physical landmark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is located close to an open pit mine and there is an extension of the iron ore mine, the Omarska extension of that mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. If we return to Exhibit 108 -- let me ask you this question first. The iron ore mine, I take it, that is located next to or in the vicinity of iron ore or iron ore pits. Are those shown on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are. I see that by accident I placed an arrow on the map, that was just my ignorance, but if I can move this, there are open pit mines in this area here. I may remind for convenience that this is the second largest iron ore mine in Europe so it is quite a large mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The portion of the mine that was turned into a camp, what did that consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It consisted of an administrative area and a huge garage or, rather, it was almost like a hangar. The compound as such had actually five buildings; the one administrative building in which there was a canteen and the first floor with offices; this huge garage which was for maintenance of the heavy equipment used in the mine; a seemingly a tiny little building which was the "white house" and then there was another small building called the "red house" and a small pump station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who operated the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was called a military investigation centre. It was run in co-operation between the police and the military, that is, the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were only men taken to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Primarily men, but there were 36, 37, 38 women in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What age groups were taken to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was with reference to women or with reference to the male?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The overall population. Let us start with men.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men were those between 12, 15 and 60, 65, essentially.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When did Omarska begin to function as a detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is referred to by the Serbs themselves as having operated from 25th May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were held there at any given time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The numbers have varied. I think it had an absolute maximum capacity, somewhere about 3,000, 3300 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about the general conditions of the camp, and the general conditions in which the prisoners there were held. First of all, let me ask you about into what spaces the prisoners were put, how much space was there for the prisoners who were placed in areas or rooms of the former mine complex? A.This varied over time but, initially,people were extremely cramped and, that is to say, it is described as if they were sardines in a tin. They would have to stand. They could not turn around and they would stand like this for a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the prisoners provided with any bedding or blankets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were provided with nothing in terms of bedding and blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So they sat or slept on bare floors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much food did the prisoners get?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They got food once a day, one-eighth of a bread is what they referred to, and a ladle full of some soup-like fluid and possibly with some cabbage or macaroni in it and some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was this a diet sufficient to sustain a person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners fed immediately upon arrival?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they would frequently face a period of three, four, five days when they were only cramped in with no water and no food.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did the camp operate, through portions of the summer of '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was actually closed 5th/6th August, essentially, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is the summer hot in the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The summer is said to be very hot in the Prijedor area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How much water was available to the prisoners and what was the quality of that water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not pure water; it was water generally available in the mine and it was very limited water made available to them. So all water they had, essentially, went for drinking and no cleaning purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about facilities for personal hygiene; were they provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were very few such facilities. There were a few toilets which were not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did prisoners attend to their personal needs in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would, essentially, be showed to the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could the prisoners leave their rooms when they needed to and use whatever facilities were available for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Over time did the prisoners begin to suffer from medical conditions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did; malnutrition, diarrhoea, lice, very soon different diseases became rife, particularly it was very difficult to disinfect any wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was regular medical care provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no regular medical care or medical care to any degree. There were some prisoners who were doctors and they tended to fellow prisoners if they could, but, essentially, with no implements, no medicine, no disinfectant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were interrogations conducted in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. I think that is also indicated by the main intelligence centre.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Indicated by the main?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you repeat that? I think you were not heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, this was a military investigation centre, so if investigations are carried out, it in a sense followed from that they were likely to want to do some kind of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that connection, could I have Exhibit 92 presented to the witness? (To the witness): Were interrogations conducted at all three camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were, but the tougher interrogations were in Omarska and Keraterm where the men were held. I may just add, that some men ended up in Keraterm, sorry, in Trnopolje, but it seems that was if an individual Serb would help them, or if there were so cramped conditions they could not possibly be put into one of the two other camps. So, in principle, the males were taken to Keraterm and Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the Serbian officials have a designation or name for the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they referred to them as "informative talks".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that in conversations with journalists and people from outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and in conversations with journalists and aid personnel and in their own newspaper articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do we have an indication, according to the Serbian officials, at any rate, how many informative talks were conducted in the camps in the summer of 92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to Simo Drljaca, the head of the Serbian police, 6,000 such talks were held in these camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to display Exhibit 92 on the monitor looking at the second paragraph from the bottom, the first sentence? That is an interview with Simo Drljac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is again, yes, the one interview he gave when he had been appointed to be Vice Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Indicating that more than 6,000 informative talks were held at the three camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Police at this time ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- at the time the camps were in operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for the entire length of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was it that actually conducted the interrogations or informative talks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was interrogators coming from outside and most of them belonged to the police, but they would have people with them who would also be army related personnel. It is said as being a military centre, but some of the investigators, that is, came from the public security office, the office of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In what manner were the interrogations conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In very brutal manners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, could you speak a bit louder because I have difficulty hearing. I believe Mr. Orie too has difficulty hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really apologise because ......

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I will repeat the question, your Honour. (To the witness): In what manner were these interrogations conducted, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In very brutal manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were severely beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they tortured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many were severely tortured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the statements extracted from the prisoners during these informative talks later used to justify both their imprisonment and the cleansing of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that regard, can I ask you to look at Exhibit 91, to be presented to the witness? Can page 2, the second full paragraph, be displayed on the monitor? Dr. Greve, this issue of Kozarski Vjesnik contains an account of how the first Chairman of the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, Dr. Milomir Stakic, saw the events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that first sentence of the second paragraph does he indicate what happened after the prisoners were taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is indicating that enough information was gathered from them to conclude that the Muslims were very well organised and determined to liquidate their fellow citizens, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So after the prisoners were taken into custody, that information was gathered, according to Mr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking three sentences past that in the sentence which begins, "From the interrogation records ... "?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is claimed that they learned, the Serbs learned, that they, meaning the non-Serbs, had intended to simultaneously take over power and seize the barracks and with it the arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What else was learned during those interrogation sessions, according to Mr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Worst of all, according to him, the Serbs found out that the Muslims had a detailed plan for the liquidation of the Serbian population of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the interrogation records extracted from prisoners during these brutal interrogations then produced the information that Mr. Stakic was talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to beatings during interrogation, Dr. Greve, were prisoners subjected to physical abuse at other times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were subjected to physical abuse when they went to the canteen to get their food, when they could be beaten at any one time, to the extent that prisoners, although they needed the food badly, had to consider whether they were in a shape to go to fetch their food. Similarly, if they needed to relieve themselves, they had to consider if it was safe to do that considering who were the guards on duty because they were also subjected to beatings on such occasions. A number of prisoners who at night-time slept in the canteen would stay outdoor. It is called a pista. It is a concrete platform between the administrative building and a huge garage. When they were staying there, they could also be randomly subjected to ill-treatment. Particularly at night-time, people would come to where the prisoners were kept and ask for a few names and take them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This was just regular shift guards who subjected prisoners to such beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were people from inside and outside the camp, police, military, paramilitary, locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any particular type of people, people from any particular segment of society, more at risk in Omarksa than others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for (1) it seems to have been the tendency that in Omarska the upper echelons or the elite of the non-Serbian community was gathered and, particularly, the elite, meaning people who held important positions in the community, politicians and leaders, everything from people who were good football players and onwards would be particularly subjected to ill-treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any particular parts of the camp more dangerous for prisoners than others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The by far most dangerous part of the camp was the seemingly small white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened in the white house that made it more dangerous or were special people put in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, people were frequently put in the white house upon interrogation, if they had survived the interrogation, and they were subjected to possibly the most extreme of the ill-treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What treatment were the women who were held in Omarska subjected to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one level they had better conditions than the male population. However, for them the main problem was rapes at night-time, and it happened almost all the time, it is being reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, were prisoners killed in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a number of prisoners were killed in Omarska. It is difficult to establish the exact numbers, but the fact that, according to Serb officials, there were no large scale releases and considering the numbers who were taken to the camp, it must have been a substantial number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: By "substantial" do you mean dozens, tens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would rather suggest thousand or more, but I am not in a position to establish numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were these killings of prisoners secret ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- kept by the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not secret, that is to say, interrogation took place in closed offices and the white house had closed doors and was a compound on its own. However, dead prisoners would be left outside so that other prisoners going to relieve themselves, going to fetch their food or staying on the pista, that is, the concrete platform in day time, would be able to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the camp a secret? Did local Serbian leaders know about it or not know about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was no secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they ever visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some of them did visit the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about Simo Drljaca, the chief of police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did visit the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Serbian officials from outside opstina Prijedor visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did from Banja Luka. It is also my understanding that Radio Televizija Banja Luka came to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about the ICRC or humanitarian organisations, were they able to visit and inspect the camp during its operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As long as Omarska was operated this way that is being described now, they never visited the camp. When it was being closed down and given beautification or shined up for foreign journalists to come in, also ICRC was entitled to come to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was the camp closed or when did it begin to close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an article in the American press, 2nd August, and subsequent to that it was an immediate effort made to close the camp, transfer prisoners. It was basically closed on 5th and 6th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the camp's existence was made known to the western world, did journalists try to enter the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were some journalists able to enter the camp around the time period you have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but only after the main group of prisoners had been removed and a lot of clean up had been made and then only to a very limited area of the camp -- essentially the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the majority of prisoners from Omarska transferred at that time, end of the first week of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the vast majority or possibly they were left 100 or some more than 100 but .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
