utterances.text: The majority was most probably taken to Manjaca. Manjaca is a camp which is located in opstina Banja Luka, to my understanding. I have not focused much on that particular camp, but it has been referred to by the Serb authorities. But also maybe more than 1,000 were taken to Trnopolje which was kept open after the time when Omarska was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Although I appreciate that you have not focused on Manjaca extensively, do you know whether or not conditions in Manjaca were the same as in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was far better. It was not that dangerous. It was the likelihood of survival.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did some prisoners remain behind in Omarska after the majority of prisoners were transferred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as the camp was being showed to the international media, they were the ones to be paraded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they responsible for cleaning up the camp and making it as presentable as possible when the media came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these men who were left behind, and also the women before they were transferred, were asked to do some of the cleaning. Three women were left behind initially, but when the press came it was denied that there were any women in the camp and they had been taken out in a car to Omarska at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Serbian officials connected with the operation of the camp questioned about the nature of the camp after the journalists discovered it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they questioned, in particular, about whether or not prisoners had been beaten or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were questioned about this.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When did you testify that you believed journalists learned about the camp? You said that it was closed in August, August 4th or 5th, I believe, 1992, and that would have been shortly after they learned. So when do you believe that they first learned about the camp and came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first article written about the issue which was well-known was Roy Gutman's article published in Newsday, I believe, in the United States, 2nd August 1992. Then things happened very, very quickly because prior to that it had been alleged that camps existed, and now pressure was put on Radovan Karadzic to let journalists into the specific locations in Prijedor. So it happened very, very quickly, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked for identification as Exhibit 109, please? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what is Exhibit 109?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a transcript from an interview where Stakic is making statements concerning, inter alia, Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 109 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May that be displayed on the monitor, please? (To the witness): First of all, does Milomir Stakic indicate at whose direction or upon whose decision the camps were set up? I would direct your -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does. In the second paragraph he is saying that this was done at the decision -- on the decision of the Prijedor Civil Authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Milomir Stakic asked about beatings in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is saying that, according to the information, there was no maltreatment and physical violence in the centres themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was he confronted about reports of killing in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was, and said, "There were cases, as the Commander in charge let me know, of death which all have medical documentation which testifies to that and not to murder".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does he indicate that he is referring to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does. He is particularly asked if this was in Omarska and he confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does he say that in any event the number of prisoners who died of natural causes was small?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said that he is unable to say exactly, but it was not a large number. He is asked again if it was not many people and he says, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was this denial of beatings in Omarska always consistently maintained by the de facto officials of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this marked as Exhibit 110 for identification? (Document handed). What is Exhibit 110, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is again a transcript from an interview this time with Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A member of Krizni Stab?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was or may still be, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this interview is he also asked by Omarska and physical mistreatment in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 110 will be admitted. Mr. Tieger, you asked Dr. Greve if he was a member of what? Chris?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Krizni Stab or Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That brings to mind that we have, perhaps, not focused on the establishment of the Krizni Stab. I think we left that out. If your Honours would like, I am happy to briefly describe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It may be more convenient to finish this section of the examination and pick it up after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is fine. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Can we focus on the bottom part of the page? Is Mr. Kovacevic asked about the situation in Omarska and investigations of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Is he confronted by a reporter who was told that some men had been investigated because of Omarska, some prison guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How does he respond to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is saying that there were some mistakes. He accepts that some mistakes have been discovered, and then he moves on to say that war is war and some people got drunk, and then he is being interrupted by the interpreter. And "Of course, we condemn it and we are working to solve it. Some of the men have been imprisoned already".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the reporter press on to find out how many people have been imprisoned for mistakes in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does Kovacevic tell him on page 2 of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is saying that this is not his field of work. His field is economy, and he does not know how many they are, but they do exist, according to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Kovacevic interviewed on another occasion about Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is -- I think on many other occasions than this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 111 for identification? (Document handed) (To the witness): What is document 111, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is again an interview where Mr. Kovacevic is answering questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is he answering questions about Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that for admission, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 111 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): In this interview Mr. Kovacevic is asked about how many people died on the Serbian side and how many on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What is it that he starts talking about at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At this point he makes a reference to Jasenovac which was mentioned yesterday as being the most notorious of the death camps during World War II located in Croatia. Here a comparison is made with Auschwitz.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does he indicate that it is impossible to know even at this late date exactly how many people, Serbs in that case, were murdered in Jasenovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is indicating that even after 50 years they are still unable to say how many people were killed in Jasenovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: In the question of how many people were killed, in this interview, does Mr. Kovacevic spontaneously raise the issue of the deaths camps to explain why it is so difficult to approximate numbers or estimate numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is his comparison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We are just about to show the video, your Honour, but it is all three clips, it will probably consume about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then we will stand in recess for 20 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Just before the recess we were about to play the video clips from which the transcripts were taken. Before that is played, can we give the court three copies of those transcript exhibits? (Documents handed) Your Honour, are they marked by an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: At the top upper right-hand corner they have your numbering, I think, whatever, 4/227. I see. I have Exhibit 110, 111 and then a page with nothing, 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There were stickers on them before. The order should be a one page interview with Stakic, a two-page interview with Kovacevic and then a small, single paragraph or a brief interview with Kovacevic again. Can we then show tape clips 2, 3 and 4? (Tape clips 2, 3 and 4 were played). Can you play No. 4, please? Thank you. Your Honour, I tender document the video as No. 112 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 112?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 112 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, you mentioned that some of the Serbian officials we saw were members of the Crisis Staff. Could you tell the court whether or not the Crisis Staff was an organ of the de facto Serbian government in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in opstina, in Srpska opstina Prijedor, the Crisis Staff was sort of the Crisis Headquarters. It was composed of the leading military people, the head of the police and the leading members of the SDA, in addition, one of the directors of the mine, key people, that is, from different aspects of society to make it possible to co-operate closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, you mentioned that those persons who were rounded up after the attack on Kozarac were sent to Omarska, Keraterm and Trnpolje depending upon sex and perhaps other factors. Where was Keraterm located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Keraterm is located within the town of Prijedor. It is within the vicinity of the town centre. It is this former ceramic tiles factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could show us on Exhibit 79?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the clay -- it is called on the map "clay production plant". It is located here, in the main buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was it established and run by the same authorities who established and operated Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately how many Muslims or Croats or non-Serbs were held in Keraterm plant at any given time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At a maximum, approximately 1,500. May I also say that there were the occasional Serb who was taken to Omarska and Keraterm if they tried specifically to assist their non-Serbian fellows.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were the conditions in Keraterm camp, the crowding, the lack of food and absence of hygiene and sanitary facilities, similar to those you have described briefly in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More or less the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were prisoners also beaten and killed in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any incidents in which particularly large numbers of prisoners were killed at any one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was one particular incident. In this camp, it is one main building and there are different halls, one called hall No. 3. The night between 25th and 26th of July, it is believed that at least 150 people were machine gunned down in the night, and when their dead bodies were removed, the wounded were taken out with the dead, and possibly it could have been numbers like 60 or 80 wounded among them. That is indicated on -- I am not exactly sure of the numbers, but this was an event which was given much attention. It was considered a massacre. I would like to draw your attention to the fact that there is the main road running just by this camp, so actually people could see from the main road, look into, not the inside of the camp, but at least the camp compound, and roads were blocked following this incident as the cleaning up was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were other prisoners who were killed in Keraterm murdered by bullet in the same way or were there other forms of killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the rest of those killed were mainly killed by beatings or stabbings or a combination of this, not so much by bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Can you show us where Trnopolje camp is located, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, on this map Trnopolje is not listed by name, but as Stanica Kozarac, that is to say, the station of Kozarac, but it is also -- the village of Trnopolje, it is also located here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was Trnopolje camp run by the same authorities whom you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Essentially, yes, but also the by then Serbian local Red Cross played an important role in running of this camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Who was the head of Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the man previously referred to as head of the TO, SDS member, Slobodan Kurozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: That is the man who later was placed in charge of some aspect of Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did the function of Trnopolje camp differ in any way from that of Omarska and Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did; its main function was to be a staging area for deportations,so in this respect it is conveniently located next to the railroad station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Who was held in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was what briefly may be called the women's group with the children and the elderly men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: In general, how were conditions in Trnopolje compared to Omarska and Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Much, much, much better. But still it was a concentration camp and there were many difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was there physical abuse of prisoners from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Of what type?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, beatings, some arbitrary killings and for the women rape was the perhaps most important problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Can you return to Omarska and Keraterm camps for a moment? Is there any indication what was intended for the prisoners of Omarska and Keraterm had the international press not discovered and exposed those camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is indicated well by the head of police, Simo Drljaca, once again in the interview he gave, because at that time in April of 1993 he is indicating that it was only due to pressure from the western world that those whom he labelled extremists, fundamentalists, etc. did not got their right punishment, indicated that would be the most severe punishment possible, or existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention to Exhibit 92, please? Looking at the second to last paragraph -- first of all, is this an interview with Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does he indicate in his interview that more than 1500 Muslims and Croats had been proven through proper documentation to have actively participated in conflicts against the army of the Serb Republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: In the context of this article and other statements from Serbian officials, does that proper documentation refer to the interrogations, the "informative talks"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It is also listed two lines above.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Based on those "informative talks" and the information extracted from them, what other crimes were these 1500 Muslims and Croats believed to be guilty of by Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Participating in the genocide of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does he complain that Serb officials were not permitted to impose just punishment on those Muslims and Croats who had been proven to have participated in genocide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read the last sentence to state that, yes. The last sentence in the paragraph, that is, "Instead of receiving their just punishment, the white world mighty men forced us to release them all from Manjaca".

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. By the time the camp was discovered and prisoners were transferred to Manjaca and Trnopolje from Omarska, what were their physical states by that time, in general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People had lost considerable weight. As we will come back to, there were two main occasions on which males were brought to Omarska and Keraterm. It was after the attack on the Kozarac area and the immediate following attack on Prijedor town, and it was in late July, after 20th July, when the Ljubija area became surrounded and attacked and ethnically cleansed, so-called. That is, some people had been in the camps since late May/early June and many of them had lost weight, 20 or 30 kilos, or even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to tender a photograph for admission which has been presented to the Defence. It is No. 113. It is photo 5/1/04.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 113, there is no objection to Exhibit 113? That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can that be displayed on the elmo, please? (To the witness): Dr. Greve, is that a photo of a prisoner who had recently been released from Omarska by the time the photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if it is correct to say "released". He had been transferred to Trnopolje but he had been a detainee of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This depicts his condition immediately or shortly after his transfer from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had asked you about the difference in the primary function of the camps in Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje. You indicated that Trnopolje camp served the function of deportation centre as well. What happened to the majority of the prisoners who were held at the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority were deported out from opstina Srpska, opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Through what means were they deported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not able to say if the majority were deported by rail or road, but these were the two main used. It is reported that up to 25 cattle wagons at a time would be placed at the railway station in Banja Luka when in transit. So at least a large number did leave by rail and, essentially, by cattle wagons -- like it was used during deportations in World War II in Europe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I have this marked for identification as Exhibit 114? (Document handed). (To the witness): Dr. Greve, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a communication to the press by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is dated 2nd October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender document 114 for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 114 will be admitted. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, does Exhibit 114 reflect one of the evacuations of prisoners from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and now we have moved on in time, that is to say, that this is an evacuation; it is not a deportation. This is the time when the International Committee of the Red Cross has been granted access to some camps, including Trnopolje, and they are asking to be entitled to evacuate people out, among them a number of those who had been released also from previously from Omarska and Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Was the release of prisoners from Trnopolje either by deportation in the earlier stage or by evacuation once the ICRC conditioned on the relinquishment of anything by the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had to sign a special document where they relinquished all their material goods, moreover agreed not to return to Srpska opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as 115 for identification? (Document handed). (To the witness): What is that document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a quote of article 11 from an agreement on the release and transfer of prisoners which was made on 1st October 1992. The quote as such was included in my study, but it is taken, I had at that time the original agreement -- that is a photocopy of the original agreement -- at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender document 115 for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 115 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: We have difficulties in keeping track of the -- would there be a copy available for us because we cannot trace this exhibit at this moment? (Document handed) Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection to 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Still no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is still admitted then. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Dr. Greve, referring to 115, Article 11 is an agreement reached with which parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is suggested and proposed by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is entered into and signed by the different parties participating in the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is also a representative of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Does Article 11 reflect an understanding by ICRC officials that the release of prisoners from Trnopolje camp was dependent upon their giving up property voluntarily, and any right of return voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether the understanding of the ICRC is linked to what they had experienced by then in Trnpolje or if it is based on their general understanding of what was happening, because it was a practice which we have come across, the Commission of experts came across, all over Bosnia-Herzegovina where areas were ethnically cleansed. Possibly the ICRC could build on information from any one area in this respect. But it speaks to the fact that ICRC was aware that two categories of people, prisoners who were to be released or transferred and civilians, would be asked to sign this kind of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: OK, so this practice was not limited to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Article 11 reflects a general understanding of the use of that practice in camps throughout Bosnia

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At least it reflects this as being a widespread problem and it is general in the way it is made, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did prisoners in Trnopolje execute such documents in order to be released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they were also advised to do so by ICRC because it was a precondition for leaving, so the International Committee of the Red Cross actually advised people to sign in order to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Did all of those who were deported from Trnopolje during its operation for the ICRC intervention make it to safety after they left the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not. There were two main obstacles. It was the conditions during transportation, the lack of fresh air, water and food, it could take some days, and the least healthy ones would not always make it, babies, elderly people. At the end of the transport, the deportees would normally be asked to continue walking and frequently they would have to cross the frontline which was mined and there would be shooting above their heads and occasionally at a group of people walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any particular incidents in which large numbers of deported prisoners or evacuated prisoners did not make it to safety?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is one particular incident in which it may, perhaps, be useful, if I may suggest so, to have back again the general map of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that it could be pointed out in which direction the peoples were moved?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Certainly. If we could have Exhibit 78 shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As can be seen on this map, from Prijedor the railroad goes to Banja Luka and it continues the way to Doboj, and from this area it continues further down. Frequently people were just taken by rail a little further on from Doboj and then asked to proceed on foot in the direction -- I am sorry, I need to read the map more carefully. Some would move towards Tuzla, others would move towards Zenica. In the direction of Zenica, however, people were also deported by road, and then they will go from Banja Luka on the road in the direction of Zenica and/or rather to Travnik first. These were areas in Central Bosnia controlled by the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. When moving down on road, you will see a place called Skender Vakuf -- it was also pointed out as being an opstina -- and the road moves on, and a little further to the south and east of Skender Vakuf, there is a mountain called Vlasic. On this mountain, 22nd about of August, as I seem to remember, possibly some 250 or 300 males deported by road were taken out of the column of deportation vehicles and moved up on the mountain, the prisoners or the deportees. These were, essentially, people who had been detained in Keraterm, some in Omarska. They were asked to move out and on to the edge of a cliff, to kneel down and were shot down. Very few, maybe four, five, six, that we have been able to trace, survived. But this incident is also, to some extent, documented by the fact that it took place outside of opstina Prijedor and the military Commander, the Serb military Commander, in the place where it happened was not pleased to have this number of prisoners killed within his area of responsibility. So, they were virtually all shot down at the side of the cliff, down the cliff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, you indicated that these camps were put in active operation after the attack on Kozarac which occurred on May 24th. Did the cleansing of the Muslim and Croat communities of opstina Prijedor end with the attack and collection of citizens from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not, and one may also add that it did not only start with the attack on Kozarac, because at the same time, from mid May 1992, some members of the elite were individually rounded up and sorted out in Prijedor town as well and when the main cleansing had taken place in the Kozarac area, it continued for some time as some people had been able to hide in some shelters in nearby small villages and hamlets, but their fate was no better than that of the others. Possibly, the killings of those who were not rounded up immediately, more of them possibly percentage-wise were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: In Prijedor town itself, or within the opstina, was there any coordinated act of resistance against the coup leaders in the takeover of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from within Prijedor town, but if I may exchange the maps?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Which one do you want to put on?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think you need Exhibit 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe 79 is the map which the court has copies of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map we have Prijedor town and we have the Sana River and we have the left bank of the Sana River. We have the village Hambarine which was attacked prior to Kozarac, and we have a forested area called Kurevo to which some people had been retreating. Among them were some people who organised an armed resistance led by a Croat named Slavko Ecimovic who later died in Omarska. Approximately 150-strong this group launched an attack on Prijedor town to regain power from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How successful was that attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That attack was without any success at all. That is, maybe they thought they would have support from within Prijedor, but they had no support. They were not well-armed and they were routed and driven out again, some killed within a few hours. They came through across the Sana River and then through the old part which is called Stari Grad of Prijedor town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I direct your attention to Exhibit 93? Looking at the bottom of Exhibit 93, does it refer to the effort by these 150 or so people to regain Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. They are being referred to as green berets which again is a reference to Muslim military or paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that the people who carried out the attack were not particularly well-armed. Did they have any heavy weapons, any armour, any artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not have anything but handguns, machine guns and possibly some grenades, possibly grenade launches, but they had no artillery or any heavy equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were all of them armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of them were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As they could not find the needed number of arms, and also most probably because they thought when coming into town possibly some of them would be able to assist them, that they might be able to kindle some kind of rebellion, but that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: According to the Serbian authorities, how long did it take to defeat these 150 poorly armed people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then the attack was over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then the attack was over, from the attackers' side that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Were announcements made on Radio Prijedor about the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, announcements were made in the early morning on Radio Prijedor, essentially telling the people to stay indoors, to keep calm and not be afraid because this would soon be controlled by the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were Muslims or Croats of Prijedor advised to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were advised to put up sheets of white material, blankets or whatever they would find, to mark their house and to indicate that they had surrendered or were loyal to the Serb authorities in Prijedor town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened in portions of Prijedor that day after Muslim and Croat citizens, or at least those who received the word, put white flags out of their windows to identify their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A number of quarters in Prijedor were this very morning ethnically cleansed, that is, the incoming Serb armed groups, army paramilitary, police and locals, would after having reported the attackers go on and ask all non-Serbs living in houses that had been marked in this manner to come out into the streets, and again they would subdivide them into these two categories: the male group between 12-15, 60-65, and the women's group, who were the children and the elderly men. They would move them then on, men again to Keraterm and Omarska, and women to Trnopolje. I should perhaps add that at this time it was so cramped everywhere that it was very difficult to find room for people. So some of the women's group were taken to a gymnasium, a sports hall, Mladost, in the city itself which also served as a staging area. Others were initially detained in schools just for there to be enough space in the three camps proper for the different categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were any portions of the Prijedor town destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the one portion that was particularly destroyed was the Stari Grad, meaning the old city, and the old city is located next to the Sana River and then it is on all other sides surrounded by a canal. It is said to have had particularly old, beautiful and Muslim dominated architecture, and it was almost raised to the ground. Reportedly there were afterwards only a few buildings left. But not all the buildings were destroyed in the attack. It was followed up later, being raised to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the cleansing of Muslims and Croats continue in other parts of the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did continue. I should hasten to add that in this period after Kozarac region had been cleansed and the town of Prijedor had been cleansed, I believe, if for nothing else, logistical purposes it was impossible to take on cleansing of further areas immediately. But cleansing went on in villages, hamlets, separate houses in the manner that they would come to a house, arrest an individual and they would put very hard pressure on the remaining population. This was the time when they were also asked to wear a white arm band to distinguish themselves when they went out to the streets. Virtually any Serb could go to a home of any non-Serb and demand whatever they liked, be it property, be it for the women to join them. No one had any protection, legally speaking, any more if they were non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were and where did the last major cleansing take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last major cleansing was concentrated on the one remaining main area with non-Serbian population, that is the Ljubija area, the Hambarine area, the Kurevo forest. All that is on the west bank of the Sana River.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we show Dr. Greve Exhibit 79 again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This again is the Sana River. This is the left bank of the Sana River. This is Ljubija. This is Hambarine. I should also perhaps point out some other names that you will probably hear again from witnesses: Rakovcani, Ecimovic, Biscani and Carakovo. This entire area is frequently referred to as "Brdo" meaning mountain. It is a mountainous forested area. Ljubija is again one large extension of this main mining complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately how many non-Serbs were in the area when this last major cleansing took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is estimated to have been approximately 20,000 altogether. I should add that moving south of Ljubija we still have some part of opstina Prijedor, and these were areas essentially inhabited by Croats. There were only 5.6 per cent Croats in the opstina according to the census of 1991, and many of them were living in the Ljubija area and to its south.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I can have the elmo panned back in the direction of the area between Prijedor and Kozarac. I would like to move you chronologically through the period of time which you have described this afternoon leading up to the last major cleansing in the Hambarine area. You already indicated that the first attack took place in Hambarine and then the next day moved on to the Kozarac area which is depicted here. Did some of the residents of the Kozarac region, which included that broader area you showed us, flee in various directions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they tried to flee in various directions, but it was again extremely difficult for them to get out. Some were eventually rounded up as they tried to climb the mountain and get over it to the northern side of the Kozara mountain. Some were actually also rounded up by UN and handed over to the Serbs. Some of them tried to go into other areas. When it was cramped in Trnopolje at one point it was decided that some of the women and children could go out again and stay with relatives. Some of these relatives lived in a predominantly Muslim suburb to Prijedor named Puharska and others would go to a village named Cela which is across the fish lake, fish farm from Kozara, and a number may have also tried to get into Ljubija area. But their freedom of movement was severely restricted at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Over the succeeding weeks following the attack on Kozarac, was the area systematically cleansed of Muslims and Croats piece by piece and village by village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost house by house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would include the area we see south of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would include all the areas that we see here. When we come over to, for instance, the area of Orlovci or in this direction we find more Serb dominated areas, but essentially it may be said that every single village and hamlet and settlement was cleansed for the non-Serbs. It should also be mentioned that before the main attack on the Kozarac area and later on the left bank of the River Sana and also before Stari Grad was attacked by the Muslims, the Serbs one way or another had been alerted and were out or primarily out. Of course there were the occasional people who did not want to move.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, just for the record, what do you mean by "cleansed"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may perhaps, first of all, apologise for using this term. It is a euphemism. "Ethnically cleansed" means by armed force or violence, being rounded up. If one survives this rounding up, it means being transferred to camps such as Omarska or Keraterm for the males and for the women to be ready for deportation. It means there is no room for them any more in Srpska opstina Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During this period of time from May 24th, actually from May 23rd until the attack on the Hambarine area in July, did some people attempt to flee in the direction of the Hambarine area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then when did this last major attack take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It started on 20th July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did that attack begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again the area was bombarded and then it obviously had been surrounded as troops were moving in from all their front directions. With "troops" I refer to ordinary military forces, Reserve troops as well. I refer to paramilitary groups. I refer to police units and Reserve Police and I refer to some occasional local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the bombardment, that is when those units moved in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is when those units moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did this cleansing action differ in any respect from those which had preceded it in Hambarine in May and in Kozarac in May and in the smaller cleansings that followed A.It is difficult to establish exactly,but possible on-the-spot killing was happening to a larger extent in this last killing, excuse me, than in these previous cleansing operations. I do not know if it has anything to do with the fact that there were still many prisoners both in Omarska and in Keraterm, and now when they had rounded up prisoners they seem to find no place to put them. So there are reported bus loads of killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am not clear in what area this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour. If we can refer back to Exhibit 79. I apologise for departing from the map. Dr. Greve, you had indicated Kozarac and then the areas of the intermittent and systematic cleansings which took place thereafter. Now you have just been discussing the last major cleansing. Can you direct the court's attention to where that took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is in the Hambarine-Ljubija area. It is on the left bank. Maybe we can have some details of the map, first to the north of Hambarine. Actually, everything from Prijedor and up in this direction, or actually on the left bank of the River Sana, there is another area which is cleansed in smaller operations later, and that is on the east bank of the River Sana and the fish pond. But at this time it is from Prijedor town up to approximately this Biscani, Hedici and down again all over the Ljubija area and all the areas between the River Sana and the roads. This is the main road. This is the main road leading down to Sanski Most. It is also known that troops, the 6th Sana Brigade, for instance, came from Sanski Most to participate in this cleansing operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were those Muslims and Croats who survived the shelling or the invasion of troops taken after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The male groups were taken to Keraterm and Omarska. The women's group, children and elderly men, were taken to Trnopolje. Some may have been deported straight from an athletic field that was to be built in Tukovi which is a suburb to Prijedor town on the left bank of the River Sana.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ultimately, if they survived the camps, to be deported from opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned one of the contingents of military forces which participated in the last cleansing action against Hambarine. I would like to ask you about some of the military forces which participated in the cleansings which you have described in Kozarac and Hambarine and so on. Can we learn from Serbian officials themselves some of the military units which participated in these cleansings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we can as they are celebrating this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In that regard I would like to direct your attention to this exhibit which I would ask to be marked as No. 116 for identification what is this document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is again a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik dated 20th May 1994. It is headlined: "To the Pride and Honour of the Fatherland".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that an article which occurs in honour or which is written in honour of the day of 43rd Prijedor Motorized Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 116 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, turning to page 3, the second paragraph, does the article indicate where the 43rd Motorized Brigade participated in actions in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It refers to Prijedor which, from the context, must be the town of Prijedor, Kozarac, Kurevo, the forested area on the left bank of the River Sana that is, Panjik, Hambarine and what is referred to as other Mujaheddin strongholds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did units of the 43rd also participate with other contingents of the Serb military forces in other clensings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is referred to participation in Novi Grad, Kljuc, Sanski Most and Krupa on the River Una.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Along with what other military units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 5th Kozara and the 6th Krajina. The 6th Krajina is the same as I previously referred to as the 6th Sana. It had its headquarters in Sanski Most which is the opstina and the town to the south of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I now direct your attention to this document which I would ask to be marked as No. 117 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe before we move I may also point out that in the next paragraph there is a reference to 5th Kozara and 6th Grmec. It is my understanding that the headquarters or a headquarters of the above mentioned 6th Krajina is at the plateau of a small mountain called Grmec, meaning that it is the same unit as it is referred to call 6th Grmec and 6th Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This again is a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik, dated 6th August 1994: Persistent in the defence of Serbian people, the war path of the 5th Kozarac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 117?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, as you indicated, this is an article on the war path of the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the article indicate why the 5th Kozarac Brigade will be created?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, is there any objection to 117?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: There is no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 117 will be admitted. Do you want to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, is there any indication why the 5th Kozara Brigade had been created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is in the first paragraph. It is specifically stated that the 5th Kozara Brigade had been created as a territorial formation within the army forces of the former Yugoslavia to carry out the warfare in the region of Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the article indicate further down on that page where the 5th Kozara Brigade conducted its operations? If I could direct your attention to the last section of that first major paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The troops and the commanding officers contributed a great deal towards the preparations of the Serbs to take control in Prijedor, as well as during cleansing of the town from the Muslim fundamentalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When does the article indicate that the 5th Kozara Brigade successfully completed its combat operations at Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 1st August 1992 as it could then move on to other obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The cleansing operations were largely completed at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I have this document marked as Exhibit 118 for identification, please? What is this document, Dr. Greve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again an article in Kozarski Vjesnik, dated 29th July 1994. It has the headline: "The Brigade of a long and honourable war path, a war path of the 5th Kozara Brigade, immense contribution to the freedom."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 118 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, may I direct your attention to the fourth page of this article, the last paragraph? Does that indicate where the 5th Kozara Brigade participated in the cleansings and with what other units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the headline "20th May 1992" it is referred that, "The Assembly in the village of Jaruge Prijedor of the first battalion consisting of the troops from Slavonia and some new recruits. Subsequent involvement in the battles for liberation of the villages of Kozarac in a joint operation with the first battalion of the 43rd Transport Brigade and parts of the 2nd Battalion of our Brigade previously gathered in the village of Gornji Garevci", that is a Serb dominated village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, does the court wish me to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, it is 5.30. I just had a question about where these troops came from. Where did they get their material and who were the troops themselves? Were they Bosnian Serbs, Serbs from the Prijedor area or somewhere else? But I suppose we can explore that tomorrow. Dr. Greve, you are excused until tomorrow at 10.00 a.m. Thank you for coming. We want to talk about the schedule for next week, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As you indicated this morning, Mr. Niemann, you had heard that there will be another matter handled by this Chamber I suppose next week. You have heard a number of things, but let me focus on that. The schedule for next week will be as follows. Much to my regret, on Monday we will not hear this case. Monday is a holiday. I just enquired what holiday it is and I was told that it is Whitsun. Anyway, it is an official holiday and government offices are closed, so we will not hear this case. Tuesday we will also not hear this case, Mr. Orie and Mr. Niemann. The Trial Chamber has another matter that it has to consider. On Wednesday we will not hear this case in the morning; this Trial Chamber has two matters it has to consider. But we will continue Wednesday afternoon of next week, as well all day Thursday and all day Friday So, to recapitulate, Monday is an official holiday, the Tribunal will be closed. On Tuesday this Trial Chamber has another matter to handle and on Wednesday we have two additional matters to handle. So we will not hear the case on Tuesday at all. On Wednesday we will begin at 2.30 of next week and we will sit all day Thursday and all day Friday. Are there additional matters, Mr. Niemann or Mr. Orie?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The court adjourned for a short time)
(The hearing adjourned until the following day)
